                                                FOREWORD
Given the new pattern of CLAT/AILET and the unchanged pattern of OLETs (Other Law Entrance Tests), one needs
to make sure not to miss out on either of the two while preparing for law entrances. Our study material, hence, is
designed to cater to all your preparation needs, not just for CLAT but OLETs as well. You’ll soon discover that the
content of these pages, combined with our online material, serves as a stupendous CLAT/OLETs-prep compendium.
A language is learned and improved by consistent exposure to current usage practices and newly emerging
patterns, across all the ‘skills’ of a language.

Test of the English language in law entrance examinations can be broadly categorized into Reading Skills,
Vocabulary, and Grammar. While it is helpful to see and study language in the popular ‘tri-bullet’ formation, it is
necessary to appreciate that no completely isolated categories are possible, as every area influences and is affected
by every other area.

The latest notification by the Consortium of NLUs guides us to expect all Reading Comprehension questions
intertwined with contextual vocabulary and grammar questions.

The English section in CLAT 2020 to 2026 was comprehension-based entirely, a set of 4-6 Reading comprehension
passages with 5-7 questions each. AILET 2022 and AILET 2026 had 50 questions on reading comprehension. So,
the best chance an aspirant has is to try and develop their language independently of the CLAT ambit.

The study material, in the form of RSMs and Mocks, will help you:
• Familiarize yourself with the test format and the test question types
• Identify the test-taking skills you most need to focus on
• Evaluate your performance and realize your stronger and weaker areas and work accordingly
• Check your progress with verbal ability and reading comprehension questions.
• Practice your test-taking skills with Mock Assignments

Performer batch Specifications: - This RSM has a plethora of classroom practice sheets from moderate to
advanced levels of difficulty. This RSM is the LAST CLASSROOM RSM hence its assignments should be taken
only in the classes under the guidance of the teachers. Its answer key will be provided to the students only in
the specific classroom sessions by the respective faculty.

We hope you find this book useful, and we would love to hear your feedback.

All the best,


Happy Learning!
